binders: Universally quantify real constants K=bulkModulus and ρ=density.
Universally quantify a system in LocalDef003 K ρ, carrying fields p=pressure and u=velocity, each a function R → R → R with spatial argument first and time argument second.
After the positivity assumptions, universally quantify every profile f: R → R in the profile-related conjunction. This profile is independent of the supplied system fields.
Every x,t in the pointwise conclusions ranges independently over all of R.
Every a,b,s,t in the integral-balance definition ranges independently over all of R; every a,b in the profile integrability condition also ranges independently over all of R.

The derivative witnesses in the system conditions and transport predicates are real numbers existentially quantified inside the quantification over each point (x,t); they may depend on that point and on the fields and parameters.
hypotheses: The supplied system carries ρ≠0 and, for every real x,t, real witnesses pt,px,ut,ux such that p(x,·) has derivative pt at t, p(·,t) has derivative px at x, u(x,·) has derivative ut at t, and u(·,t) has derivative ux at x.
Those system derivative witnesses satisfy pt+K*ux=0 and ut+ρ⁻¹*px=0 at each (x,t).
conclusions: For w(x,t)=p(x,t)-ρ*c*u(x,t), at every real x,t there exist real wt,wx that are its time and spatial derivatives at that point and satisfy wt-c*wx=0.
For every profile f: R → R, define q_f(x,t)=f(x-(-c)*t). For all real x,t, q_f(x,t)=f(x+c*t).
For the same arbitrary profile and all real x,t, q_f(x-c*t,t)=f(x).
For every profile f, q_f has both coordinate derivatives at every point and satisfies (q_f)_t-c*(q_f)_x=0 everywhere if and only if f is differentiable at every real point.

For every profile f, q_f satisfies the integral-balance predicate with flux F(z)=-c*z if and only if f is Lebesgue interval integrable between every pair of real endpoints. Explicitly, the left side requires: every q_f(·,t) is interval integrable between every a,b; every τ ↦ -c*q_f(x,τ) is interval integrable between every s,t; and, for all a,b,s,t, integral_a^b q_f(x,t) dx - integral_a^b q_f(x,s) dx = integral_s^t [-c*q_f(a,τ)+c*q_f(b,τ)] dτ.
mathematical_definitions: All fields and profiles in the target are scalar-valued. The norm and topology are the usual absolute-value norm and topology on R; scalar multiplication is real multiplication.
Real.sqrt(r) is the nonnegative square root of max(r,0). The positive parameter assumptions make c the positive square root of K/ρ.
The transport predicate T(q,v) means: for every x,t∈R, there exist real qt,qx with derivative of q(x,·) at t equal to qt, derivative of q(·,t) at x equal to qx, and qt+v*qx=0.

The integral-balance predicate B(q,F) means: for every a,b,t∈R the spatial slice q(·,t) is interval integrable from a to b; for every x,s,t∈R the time slice F(q(x,·)) is interval integrable from s to t; and for every a,b,s,t∈R the spatial-integral change equals the time integral of F(q(a,τ))-F(q(b,τ)).

Interval integrability from a to b means Lebesgue integrability on both (a,b] and (b,a]. For scalar functions this includes the corresponding measurability condition and finite integral of absolute value.
The oriented integral from a to b is the integral over (a,b] minus the integral over (b,a].
Differentiability of f means differentiability at every real point, with no requirement that its derivative be continuous.
The traveling profile with speed v is the function (x,t) ↦ f(x-v*t).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any positive real constants K and ρ and any supplied pair of real fields p,u whose coordinate derivatives exist everywhere and satisfy p_t+K*u_x=0 and u_t+ρ⁻¹*p_x=0 everywhere, set c=√(K/ρ). Then c is positive, and w=p-ρ*c*u has coordinate derivatives everywhere satisfying w_t-c*w_x=0. In addition, for every real profile f, its traveling profile at speed -c is q_f(x,t)=f(x+c*t), and q_f(x-c*t,t)=f(x) for every real x,t. This q_f satisfies the pointwise transport predicate at speed -c exactly when f is differentiable everywhere. It satisfies the integral-balance predicate with flux F(z)=-c*z, including integrability of every spatial slice and every boundary-flux time slice and the balance identity for every choice of real endpoints, exactly when f is Lebesgue integrable on every bounded interval. All these conclusions hold together.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Both parameters are constant real numbers and are assumed strictly positive. The theorem asserts nothing under these hypotheses for zero or negative K or ρ; in those cases the implication has an unsatisfied antecedent.
The system already carries nonzero density and both differential equations everywhere. The theorem is conditional on that supplied system rather than an existence theorem for prescribed data.
There is no inherent empty-system vacuity for positive parameters: constant pressure and velocity fields satisfy the supplied constructor conditions.
Space and time range over the whole real line, including negative time. There are no spatial boundaries, restricted time intervals or boundary conditions.

The system assumptions and transport predicates require separate coordinate derivatives everywhere. They do not explicitly require joint differentiability, continuity of the partial derivatives, or second derivatives.
The profile identities require no regularity at all. Differentiability and interval integrability appear in equivalences, not as assumptions on every universally quantified profile.

The profile f is not identified with p-ρ*c*u at time zero or otherwise related to the given system. The target does not assert a representation or uniqueness theorem for the supplied system's transported combination.
The integrability condition is on every bounded interval; it does not require integrability over all of R, decay, compact support or boundedness.

The integral-balance predicate is specifically a balance over every spatial interval and time interval with separately required slice integrability. The proposition does not state a distributional formulation or an equivalence to one.

Integral endpoints have no ordering restrictions. Although equal endpoints produce trivial integral identities, quantification over every endpoint pair prevents the entire balance requirement from being vacuous.
The target supplies only the combination p-ρ*c*u and speed -c. It does not assert a second transported combination, reconstruction of p and u from profiles, or a classification of all solutions.
The field names do not impose units, positivity of field values, physical admissibility or any additional physical interpretation.
